Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice S.Vishwajith Shetty
Oral Order

(Per: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice S.Vishwajith Shetty) Accused Nos.1 to 5 are before this Court
under Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagarika Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, with a prayer to quash the entire
proceedings in S.C.No.304/2024 pending before the I Additional District and Sessions Judge,
Kalaburagi, arising out of Crime No.27/2023, registered by Kalaburagi Women Police Station,
Kalaburagi, for the offence punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 354, 307, 504, 506 read with
Section 149 of Ipc and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
2. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioners and learned counsel for the respondent No.2 submits that, the dispute is between the family members.
The injured victim is wife of the accused No.1.

The dispute between the parties has been amicably settled and the parties have filed application before NC:
2025:KHC-K:841 this Court seeking permission to compound the alleged offences and also have jointly prayed to allow the petition.

4. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader submits that, the charge-sheet has been filed for non-compoundable offence and therefore, the prayer made in the application seeking compounding as well as the prayer made in the petition cannot be granted.
5. A perusal of the material available on record would go to show that, the parties to this petition are all close relatives and members of a family.
The accused No.1 is the husband of the first informant and accused Nos.2 and 3 are the parents of the accused No.1.
Accused Nos.4 and 5 are also the relatives of accused No.1 to 3.

The dispute between the parties has been amicably settled and the parties have now filed application before this Court under Section 359 read with Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagarika Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, with a prayer to permit them to compound the charge-sheeted offence and also to quash the impugned criminal proceedings.
The said application is supported by the affidavit of the accused No.1 and his wife, NC: 2025:KHC-K:841 who is the first informant in the present case.

In the affidavit filed by the first informant at paragraph No.2 to 10, it has been stated as follows:
"(2) That I am the complainant in S.C.No.304/2024 (Crime No.27/2023 of Kalaburagi Women P.S.,) for the offences punishable U/Sec. 498-A, 323, 307, 354,
504, 506 and r/w. Section 149 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act,
against the petitioners.
That, I have filed the complaint againswt the petitioners.
That due to intervention of family members, elderly persons and well wishers of our respective families, myself and petitioners settled the dispute amicably.

Accordingly,
I and petitioner/accused No.1 are started residing together in House No.22/08, Plot No.36, Sy.No.82/1, Unity Layout, Kotnoor-D, Taluk and district Kalaburagi and leading our happy marital life since from 21.04.2024.

sentences.text: (3) I say that, in view of compromise I am voluntarily without any force, coercion and undue influence by anybody consenting to quash the criminal proceeding initiated by me as aforesaid against the petitioners.

(4) That, in view of aforesaid settlement, the present criminal petition may kindly be allowed by quashing the entire criminal proceedings in S.C.No.304/2024 (Crime No.27/2023 of Kalaburagi NC: 2025:KHC-K:841 Women P.S.) which is now pending on the file of learned I Additional District and Sessions Judge, Kalaburagi.

sentences.text: (5) That the aforesaid settlement between us will help each other to live our life peacefully and happily in future.
(6) That, in view of the amicably settlement I have n objection to quash the proceedings.
(7) That, if proceedings are quashed no prejudice or harm would cause to respective parties and the State and it would maintain harmony in society.
(8) That, the alleged offences are not heinous in nature and not against the society.
It would be in the interest of justice to quash the proceedings by accepting amicable settlement entered between respective parties.

The continuation of criminal case would put us to great oppression, prejudice and extreme injustice would be cause to me.
(9) That the amicable settlement entered between me and respondent No.2 will help both of us to live peacefully in the future.
(10) That, in view of the amicable settlement respondent No.2 has given no objection to quash the proceedings on above stated terms."

6. The parties who are before this Court have been identified by their respective Advocates and they have stated NC: 2025:KHC-K:841 that, the settlement arrived between them is voluntarily and without there being any undue influence or coercion.

They have also stated that, the parties have decided to give a quietus to the dispute between them and the accused No.1 and the first informant have decided to reside together separately in a rented premises.

7. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Ramgopal vs. The State of Madhya Pradesh1 has observed that, notwithstanding the limitations provided under Section 320 of Cr.P.C., in a given case, depending upon the facts and circumstances of the case and also the nature of the allegations and nature of the settlement arrived between the parties, this Court in exercise of its powers under Section 482 of Cr.P.C., can quash the criminal proceedings registered even for non-compoundable offences.
